algorithm: HMAC-SHA-256 (D171) or Ed25519 (O6) over canonicalBytes(message, direction): the MAC in lowercase hex, the device signature in unpadded base64url (mobile plan §3.5, D171, O6; direction by the owner ruling of 2026-10-18)
direction: the node the record is stored in (inbox, outbox or heartbeat), covered as the field "direction"; it is never stored in the record, and a reader passes the node it read from
canonical: JSON, keys sorted by code point at every depth, no insignificant whitespace, absent fields omitted, JSON's own escaping only, integers only
covered: every field except the tag it is written in (mac or sig, neither covering itself) and acked, plus the direction
key_note: a readable placeholder, not a credential: the real key is the per-pairing key of D171 and never appears in this repository

cases.name: plain message
cases.why: the ordinary message of §3.1: four fields and a tag, and the acked flag the phone writes later is not covered

cases.name: prompt with options
cases.why: a prompt reads its options aloud and the answer names one by position, so the array is covered in order (D167, §3.2)

cases.name: answer
cases.why: an answer says which prompt it settles (D168 amended: the TTL is the consumer's)

cases.name: action: cancel a run
cases.why: D169's typed destructive command: the confirmation id and time are inside the tagged bytes, never beside them

cases.name: action: merge a pull request
cases.why: a merge carries the head SHA read back at confirmation, which the consumer re-checks before it merges

cases.name: action: launch in a costly mode
cases.why: O10's typed start: the mode is the field the record exists for, and a costly mode's read-back carries the confirmation that authorises it (D2786)

cases.name: a turn: a prompt for a named agent
cases.why: P5.4.2, D161: the front agent's turn reuses the prompt kind and says which agent it is for, and the agent is covered by the tag like every other field

message.text: shall I shape this into a task?

cases.canonical: {"agent":"front-agent","at":1700000000000,"direction":"outbox","id":"m-0001","kind":"prompt","options":["make it a brief","keep talking"],"sender":"phone","text":"shall I shape this into a task?"}

cases.name: stop request
cases.why: the phone asking a human to stop what it is looking at: a kind of its own, signed like every other, and never executed by anything

cases.name: heartbeat
cases.why: O7: the consumer's liveness record, whose agent list feeds D163 — an unsigned heartbeat is offline

cases.name: registration
cases.why: P5.2.1, §3.5 (b): the app's registration-and-preferences message — the token, the platform and §3.8's switches, all of them inside the bytes the tag covers

cases.name: html characters stay raw
cases.why: Go escapes <, > and & unless SetEscapeHTML(false) is set; the tagged bytes are the raw characters

cases.name: non-ASCII is UTF-8
cases.why: an emoji is its own characters, not a \u escape, in both languages

cases.name: keys are ordered by code point, not by UTF-16 code unit
cases.why: §3.5 sorts keys by code point at every depth; U+FFFF < U+1F600 by code point and after it by UTF-16 code unit

cases.name: an unknown field is inside the bytes
cases.why: §3.5 covers a field added later by default, and omits an absent one rather than writing null

cases.name: text swapped
cases.why: the body under a tag made for another body: "merge it" spoken by an impostor

cases.name: options swapped
cases.why: an option added under a tag made for the shorter list: "option two" must not change meaning
cases.canonical: {"at":1700000000000,"direction":"outbox","id":"m-0001","kind":"prompt","options":["merge it","leave it"],"sender":"phone","text":"the pull request is green"}

cases.name: options swapped: order
cases.why: a reordered list is a different set of positions, so it is different bytes
cases.canonical: {"at":1700000000000,"direction":"outbox","id":"m-0001","kind":"prompt","options":["leave it","merge it"],"sender":"phone","text":"the pull request is green"}

cases.name: reply_to swapped
cases.why: an answer moved to another prompt under its own tag

cases.name: answer swapped
cases.why: the answer itself changed under a tag made for "option one"

cases.name: agents changed
cases.why: an impostor added to the advertised list under a tag made for the real one

cases.name: agent renamed
cases.why: the spoken name of an advertised agent changed under its tag

cases.name: target swapped
cases.why: another pull request under a tag made for this one: the read-back named a target, and the consumer must merge that one

cases.name: head SHA swapped
cases.why: the branch moved after the read-back: the head in the record is the state of the world that was confirmed

cases.name: mode swapped
cases.why: a costly start relabelled as a cheap one under the tag its read-back produced: the mode is what the session read back, so a swap has to break the tag

cases.name: brief swapped
cases.why: another task under the tag the read-back produced: the brief is what the run is started from, so a swap would start work nobody confirmed (P5.4.2)
cases.canonical: {"action":{"confirmation":{"at":1700000000000,"id":"c-0003"},"id":"a-0003","mode":"pro","target":{"repo":"dimipaun/fugaro"},"verb":"launch"},"agent":"orchestrator","at":1700000000000,"brief":"# Task: something else entirely\n","direction":"inbox","id":"m-0001","kind":"action","sender":"phone","text":"start it in pro"}

cases.name: confirmation swapped
cases.why: another confirmation id under a tag made for this one: the consumer's ledger must not be fooled

cases.name: verb swapped
cases.why: a cancel relabelled as a merge under its own tag

cases.name: inbox tag read as outbox
cases.why: a phone-signed answer copied into the outbox by a minted token: the tag was made for the inbox

cases.name: outbox tag read as inbox
cases.why: a consumer-signed message copied into the inbox: "approve the merge?" answered with the consumer's own words

cases.name: heartbeat tag read as outbox
cases.why: a signed heartbeat is not an outbox message

refusals.name: unsigned message
refusals.why: the tag is required on every inbox and outbox message (§3.5)

refusals.name: unsigned prompt
refusals.why: a prompt is signed like every other kind

refusals.name: unsigned answer
refusals.why: an unsigned answer is exactly what an impostor would send to "approve the merge?"

refusals.name: unsigned action
refusals.why: an action record without a tag is never executed

refusals.name: unsigned stop
refusals.why: a stop request is signed like every other kind: an impostor could otherwise put a stop request in the owner's name

refusals.name: unsigned heartbeat
refusals.why: an unsigned heartbeat is offline, and its agent list is ignored (O7)

refusals.name: short mac
refusals.why: a tag is exactly 64 hex characters: 63 is not a tag

refusals.name: long mac
refusals.why: 65 is not a tag either

refusals.name: uppercase mac
refusals.why: hex has one spelling here, so one tag has one string

refusals.name: null mac
refusals.why: absent is omitted, never null

refusals.name: unknown verb
refusals.why: the verbs are cancel, merge, confirm and launch, and nothing else

refusals.name: short head SHA
refusals.why: a head SHA is 40 or 64 hex characters: an abbreviation cannot be compared byte for byte

refusals.name: uppercase head SHA
refusals.why: a head SHA is lowercase, as the provider returns it

refusals.name: merge without head SHA
refusals.why: a merge carries the head it was confirmed against

refusals.name: a launch without a mode
refusals.why: a start names the mode it starts in, and the mode is the field the record exists for (O10)

refusals.name: a mode on a cancel
refusals.why: mode is a launch's field, and a cancel that carried one would be a record the consumer had to guess the meaning of

refusals.name: a launch without a target
refusals.why: every action names what it acts on, and a start names the repository it starts in

refusals.name: a launch targeting a run
refusals.why: a start starts a repository: a run is what a cancel cancels, and there is no run id before the start

refusals.name: a launch whose target carries a pull request
refusals.why: a start has no pull request to name, so a repository-and-pr target is a target the verb cannot use

refusals.name: a mode one code unit past its bound
refusals.why: a mode is a short word (64 code units), not a body: 65 is the first length that is not one

refusals.name: a mode carrying a space
refusals.why: a mode is an identity string, and a space in one is a phrase where the session expects a word

refusals.name: a head SHA on a launch
refusals.why: the head SHA belongs to a merge: a start has no branch state that was read back

refusals.name: a launch with no brief
refusals.why: a start with no brief would start a run with nothing to work from, and the brief is the one thing the front agent exists to produce (P5.4.2, question 3)

refusals.name: an empty brief
refusals.why: a brief that says nothing is a run with nothing to work from: the empty string is not a brief (P5.4.2)

refusals.name: a brief one code unit past its bound
refusals.why: a brief is bounded (P5.4.2): 16385 code units is a document, not the task a conversation shaped

refusals.name: a brief with no agent
refusals.why: a brief is the front agent's own text, so the message that carries one carries the agent it is for (D161): a brief with no agent is a brief from nobody (P5.4.2)

refusals.name: a brief on a cancel
refusals.why: a brief is a launch's field and no other verb's: a cancel acts on work that already exists, so a brief beside it is a field the consumer would have to guess the meaning of (P5.4.2)

refusals.name: a brief on a plain message
refusals.why: the brief is a message-level field the (kind, field) table admits on one kind only, so a kind that cannot carry one is refused at it rather than read as free text (P5.4.2)

refusals.why: the brief travels beside the action and never inside `action.target`, which is the repository alone: a launch whose target grew a field is a launch whose meaning changed (P5.4.2, O10)

refusals.name: a brief inside the action record
refusals.why: the action record is closed and the brief is not one of its fields: a brief written there is an unknown field rather than a second spelling of the message's (P5.4.2)

refusals.name: too many options
refusals.why: a prompt carries at most eight options

refusals.name: too long text
refusals.why: a body is at most 4096 code units

refusals.name: unknown field
refusals.why: a field the schema does not name is refused, so the field set is the version

refusals.name: __proto__ field
refusals.why: a parsed __proto__ is an unknown field, never a prototype

refusals.name: action on a plain message
refusals.why: a kind carries its own fields and no others

refusals.name: answer without reply_to
refusals.why: an answer names the prompt it answers

refusals.name: float at
refusals.why: a time is an integer millisecond

refusals.name: stored direction
refusals.why: the direction is the reader's to supply, never a field the writer stores

refusals.name: stored direction on a heartbeat
refusals.why: a heartbeat cannot claim its own direction either

refusals.name: unsigned registration
refusals.why: a registration is signed like every other kind: an unsigned one could register a device of an impostor's choosing

refusals.name: registration without a token
refusals.why: the token is the field the kind exists for (§3.5 (b): the mailbox is the only path that can carry one)

refusals.name: registration without a platform
refusals.why: §3.4's node carries the platform the token was issued for, and this message is where the principal reads it

refusals.name: options on a registration
refusals.why: a kind carries its own fields and no others

refusals.name: a token on a plain message
refusals.why: the token travels on a registration alone: on any other kind the (kind, field) table does not name it

refusals.name: a token one code unit past its bound
refusals.why: a token is bounded (the design's word): 257 code units is a body, not a registration token

refusals.name: an unknown platform
refusals.why: the platforms are ios and android, and a platform outside the pair is not one the sender can address

refusals.name: a zone that is not an IANA zone name
refusals.why: the quiet-hours zone is an IANA name, not a path and not free text

refusals.name: a zone whose later segment is a path step
refusals.why: a segment of dots alone is a path step, and the letter-first rule guards the string's first character and not the segments after it

refusals.name: a quiet-hours window whose ends are the same minute
refusals.why: a window from a minute to itself is either a whole day or none of one, and a sender that guessed would suppress the wrong hours

refusals.name: a quiet-hours minute outside the day
refusals.why: a minute of the local day is 0 through 1439

refusals.name: a quiet-hours minute that is not a whole number
refusals.why: a minute of the local day is a whole number, and a float is not one

refusals.name: a quiet-hours window missing one of its ends
refusals.why: a window is its zone and both of its ends, so a partial one would leave the consumer inventing a value the app never sent

refusals.name: an unknown field inside a quiet-hours window
refusals.why: a quiet-hours window is a closed record like every other one here

refusals.name: prefs without one of the switches
refusals.why: the message carries the whole switch state, so a partial one would leave the consumer choosing a value the app never sent

refusals.name: a switch that is not a boolean
refusals.why: a switch is true or false, and never a string the consumer would have to read

refusals.name: an unknown field inside prefs
refusals.why: §3.8's controls are a closed set like every other record here
